prompt: A carpenter checks corners by measuring three sides. Which set of side lengths makes a **right** triangle?
hint: The converse of the Pythagorean theorem: if $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$ then the triangle is right. Test the two short sides against the longest.

hints.text: The converse of the Pythagorean theorem: if $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$ then the triangle is right. Test the two short sides against the longest.

explanation: The converse says a triangle is right exactly when the squares of the two shorter sides add to the square of the longest.

alternativeExplanations.title: Carpenters really do this
steps: Builders square up a foundation by measuring $3$ ft along one edge, $4$ ft along the other, and checking that the diagonal is exactly $5$ ft.
Any multiple works, so $9$-$12$-$15$ is the same trick at triple size — handy when the corner is big.
